A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching analyses moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic SAE experiments, Gemma-2-2b sparse-probing evaluations, and an analysis of open-source SAE sparsities.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds controlled correlation experiments, JumpReLU comparisons, additional LLM configurations, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds an alternative L0-selection diagnostic based on mean absolute pairwise decoder cosine similarity (Appendix A.5). This extends the approach while retaining the original nth decoder projection calculation and automatic L0 optimization procedure, moved from v1 Appendix A.4 to v2 Appendix A.6.

E1.justification: v2 adds five-feature synthetic scenarios isolating positive and negative correlations (Section 3.1), extending v1's randomly correlated 50-feature setup. The Pile training corpus and the same sparse-probing task suite remain; additional model and layer configurations are settings changes.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates BatchTopK SAEs and ground-truth toy controls, without evaluated JumpReLU comparisons. v2 introduces extensive direct BatchTopK–JumpReLU comparisons on Gemma-2-2b layer 12 (Figures 10, 15, and 18), establishing an architectural comparison absent from v1. Appendix A.5 also evaluates decoder cosine similarity as an alternative diagnostic.

E3.justification: The Gemma-2-2b layer-12 comparison uses 1B training tokens in v2 Section 4.1, versus 500M in v1 Section 4. New protocols cover Gemma layer 5, Llama-3.2-1b layer 7, JumpReLU sparsity-coefficient sweeps, and the decoder-cosine metric. The MSE control is now described as a constructed ground-truth SAE rather than the correctly trained SAE; that description alone does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of signed correlations using ground-truth initialization, JumpReLU sparsity sensitivity, alternative-metric agreement, decoder-projection histograms, and encoder-bias/threshold dynamics (Sections 3.1, 3.6, 4.2; Appendices A.5 and A.10). These substantially expand investigation of failure mechanisms. The earlier sparsity–reconstruction and L0-transition analyses are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 reports no seed counts or uncertainty bands for its experimental sweeps. v2 specifies five seeds per L0 for the BatchTopK toy sweep and three for the additional LLM sweeps, introducing standard-deviation bands (Figures 7, 9, 13, and 14). This establishes new uncertainty reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: v2 adds results on signed feature mixing, JumpReLU's stronger high-L0 sparse-probing performance relative to BatchTopK, and cases where diagnostic minima disagree with probing optima. LLM projection and F1 curves are expanded or replaced under revised configurations and budgets, so they do not establish same-setting gains over v1. The MSE example remains 2.73 versus 4.88, and the Neuronpedia survey results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.5 introduces a mathematical definition of the decoder-cosine diagnostic, averaging absolute cosine similarities over distinct latent pairs (Equation 6). The original projection definition and automatic-L0 finite-difference updates remain unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 presents a method to determine the correct L0. v2 reframes this central contribution as a proxy that guides the search, particularly by detecting excessively low L0, and explicitly rejects treating it as a perfect guide. Its architectural scope also expands beyond BatchTopK, while retaining the central claim that insufficient L0 encourages feature mixing.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses about per-latent thresholds explaining JumpReLU's high-L0 behavior and simultaneous excessive and insufficient firing across BatchTopK latents (Section 4.2; Appendix A.10). It discusses elbows versus global minima, uncertain differences between diagnostic metrics, and limitations concerning nonlinear features and unbalanced correlations. These substantially qualify and extend v1's interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 Appendices A.1–A.3 substantially expand training-loss, pseudo-gradient, learning-rate schedule, and JumpReLU hyperparameter documentation; the code link is unchanged. Reproducibility gaps remain: toy batch size is stated as 500 in Section 3 but 1024 in Appendix A.2, and v1's explicit N(1.0, 0.15) magnitude specification is no longer supplied. These disclosure differences do not establish actual batch-size or magnitude-setting changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning around superposition and the linear representation hypothesis, nonlinear features, Anthropic's training procedure, and AxBench, citing Elhage, Park, Engels (2025), Conerly, and Wu, among others. Templeton et al.'s Scaling Monosemanticity reference is removed. The central relationship to feature hedging and absorption remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and background, expands explanations of features, latents, and toy models, and reorganizes the experimental narrative. The former appendix sparsity–reconstruction analysis becomes Section 3.4, while the discussion and appendix organization are extensively revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds correlation heatmaps, an explanatory projection histogram, architecture comparisons, and diagnostic plots, while redrawing sweep figures with uncertainty bands. Metric and probing panels are vertically aligned for comparison, and existing appendix figures move into the main text. Captions and the document template also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on one SAE architecture and one LLM layer through controlled correlation tests, JumpReLU comparisons, additional LLM configurations, and seed-based uncertainty reporting. The expanded evidence exposes failures of the global-minimum interpretation, and v2 correspondingly narrows its diagnostic claims, improving their credibility. Although conflicting toy batch-size disclosures and omitted magnitude parameters weaken reproducibility, the stronger empirical support and better-calibrated conclusions provide a clear substantial net improvement.
